Commentary.Commentary: ...The Chase...

New Zealand will be slightly disappointed. Their pacers were not upto the mark in the initial phase. They gave away a few freebies to Azam who scored a fine fifty and build a stand along with Zaman. Still, this is a par score on this pitch. The Kiwi batters are in fine form and will back themselves to chase this down. Who do you think will win? Stay tuned for the second half.

A decent performance from Pakistan but we feel they are 10-15 short. Pakistan started well and were in good position at the halfway mark. They though  fell off the track while Azam and Zaman were batting together. New Zealand pulled things back very nicely in the middle phase but in the last last three overs have away a few runs.
Two to end? Fuller and on the pads. This is worked through square leg for two. Pakistan end with 178!

Michael Bracewell says they will bowl first as feels the dew could play it's part later on. Shares they want to learn and grow on this tour and try and put up a good show. Informs they have made three changes. Tim Seifert, Cole McConchie and Zakary Foulkes are back in.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert (WK), Tom Blundell, Michael Bracewell (C), Mark Chapman, Cole McConchie, James Neesham, Josh Clarkson, Zakary Foulkes, Ish Sodhi, Ben Sears, William O'Rourke.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Saim Ayub, Usman Khan (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Iftikhar Ahmed, Shadab Khan, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Usama Mir, Abbas Afridi, Mohammad Amir.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and will bowl first.

Pakistan won the second game comfortably but New Zealand bounced back brilliantly by winning the next two games and that to in some manner. The fourth game in particular took Pakistan by surprise as they failed to chase down a par score. Credit to the tourists though, they are not here to lean back and chill but to show the world what their bench strength does possess. This is a must win for Pakistan to level the series but the Kiwis are looking to take the trophy home. We are in for a cracker for sure. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Hello and welcome to the final match between New Zealand and Pakistan. Not many would have expected the home team to see trailing against an unexpected Kiwi side coming into the final match. However, we all have been taken by surprise with how things have panned out.
...MATCH DAY...

Pakistan finds themselves trailing in the T20I series against an unexpectedly green New Zealand squad, a scenario they likely didn't anticipate before the last match. Surprisingly, the hosts suffered consecutive defeats, leaving them with the possibility of only leveling the series as the Kiwis lead 2-1, with one match washed out due to rain. Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, skipper Babar Azam, wicket-keeper Usman Khan, and all-rounder Shadab Khan are pivotal in the batting department for Pakistan. The return of Mohammad Amir has bolstered their bowling attack, forming a formidable pace duo with Shaheen Afridi, while Naseem Shah provides valuable support. Abrar Ahmed and Shahdab are key spinners in the squad. The narrow four-run loss in the last game would have stung, motivating the Pakistani players to avoid a potentially embarrassing series defeat on home soil. New Zealand, on the contrary, has displayed remarkable character and resilience, turning the tide after a setback in the second game. Tim Robinson's impressive fifty in the last match underscores his importance, alongside Dean Foxcroft, Tom Blundell, and James Neesham, who are key figures in the batting lineup. With most first-team players occupied in the Indian T20 League, New Zealand's bowling attack is makeshift. However, William O'Rourke's excellent performance in the last game, supported by Ben Sears and Jacob Duffy in the pace department, and Michael Bracewell and Ish Sodhi handling spin, has provided stability. The Kiwis aim to capitalize on their winning momentum and secure a third consecutive victory to claim a memorable series win, while the hosts are determined to prevent that outcome. The stage is set for a thrilling encounter as both teams vie for supremacy. Let's wait and watch to see who emerges victorious.
